t: Install A9 Snap, take your first screenshot, and find your way around the tray icon and the Home window. A9 Snap is a free screenshot tool for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). You press a key, then click a window, press F for the whole screen, or drag a box around part of it. The picture is on your clipboard, ready to paste, and saved as a numbered PNG file. There is no account to make and nothing to sign in to.

Install The easiest way to get A9 Snap is the Microsoft Store. It installs with no Windows warning, and Windows keeps it up to date for you. Click the badge above. A9 Snap's page in the Microsoft Store opens in a new tab. Click Get (or Install ). Windows installs A9 Snap for you. Open A9 Snap once after installing , from the Store page or the Start menu. The Store doesn't start it for you, and that first launch is when A9 Snap switches on Start at login . It opens the Home window so you can see it is running. If A9 Snap does not open, find A9 Snap in the Start menu. Already installed A9 Snap from a9snap.com? Keep using it. The Store version is a separate install with its own settings. If your work PC blocks the Microsoft Store Some work PCs do not allow the Microsoft Store. Install A9 Snap with the installer from a9snap.com instead. On a9snap.com , click Download the installer , under the Store badge. Your browser saves A9Snap-Setup-x64.exe . Open the file. Early builds are not signed with a Windows certificate yet, so Windows may show Windows protected your PC first. Click More info , then Run anyway . The Microsoft Store version avoids this step. Follow the installer. It installs for your Windows user only and does not ask for administrator rights. A9 Snap starts by itself when the installer finishes. The first time, it opens the Home window so you can see it is running.

Take your first screenshot Press Alt + Z from any app. The screen freezes and dims, and a crosshair follows your pointer. Click a window to capture it (it is outlined as you point), press F for the whole screen, or click and drag a box around what you want. A small readout shows its size, such as 640 × 220. Let go. The picture is now on your clipboard and saved in your screenshots folder. A small note at the bottom right says Copied and gives the file name. Switch to a chat, an email or a document and press Ctrl + V . To change your mind, press Esc before you let go. Take a screenshot covers windows, the whole screen, the crosshair, the magnifier and several monitors. To copy the words rather than a picture, press Alt + X instead and select the text: local OCR puts plain text on the clipboard and saves no file.

The tray icon A9 Snap waits in the tray, the row of small icons next to the clock. Its icon is the Bullseye. If you do not see it, click the ^ arrow by the clock to show hidden icons. Closing the A9 Snap window does not quit it, so the hotkeys keep working. Double-click the icon to open the Home window. Right-click the icon for the menu: Capture region , OCR capture , Recent captures , Open screenshots folder , Manual , Settings , Check for updates and Quit . A single left click shows the same menu a moment later. A small warning badge on the icon means another app has taken one of your hotkeys. See If something goes wrong . To quit A9 Snap, right-click the icon and choose Quit .

The Home window The Home window, with mock captures. Home is where you start. On the left are the Capture and Recent captures buttons, each showing its hotkey, then Editor and Folder , and a menu of settings sections. In the middle are your six newest captures. Click one to draw on it. The Home window explains every part. The Manual row under the menu opens this manual in your browser.

0.5.2 · October 30, 2026 Start at login now turns on for the Microsoft Store version. A new Store install started with the switch off (the startup task is declared off in the package and the app waited for you to switch it on), so after a restart nothing started it. It is now on for a new install, like the downloaded version, and the first launch switches Windows' startup task on; open A9 Snap once after installing. Switching it off in A9 Snap or in Windows (Settings, Apps, Startup) still works, and a policy that turned it off is shown, never overridden. The restart recovery starts the Store version through its app execution alias. The strip shows up to 24 captures and you choose the row length. Captures in the strip is 6, 9, 12, 18 or 24; the new Per row is 4, 6, 8 or 12 (default 6, so 12 captures make two rows of six). A narrow screen gets fewer to a row, and the strip scrolls: with a search or a chip on, every match is reachable by wheel, arrow keys or PageUp / PageDown. The line under the chips says "48 captures" when all of them are in the list. Thumbnails load as they scroll in. Search by app and window title. A9 Snap now notes the app and window each new capture came from (a clicked window, the window under the middle of a region, or the window you were working in for the whole screen), so typing chrome or part of a title finds it. Up to four app chips (Chrome, Outlook…) after Today, This week and Edited show the apps you capture most, and a card's tooltip says "App · title". The notes are kept in .a9snap\captures.json next to the edit originals; window titles can contain an email subject or a document's name , so they stay on this PC and never leave it. Remember which app each capture came from (Saving) turns it off, and Clear deletes what is noted. Captures from before 0.5.2 have no app.

0.5.0 · October 29, 2026 Alt+Z captures a window, the screen or a region. While the picker is up, the window under the pointer is outlined in Volt with its title and its size. Click to capture that window, cut from the frozen screen by its visible frame (no invisible resize border; a maximized window is the monitor's work area). 0.3.6 · October 27, 2026 A9 Snap is packaged for the Microsoft Store. The release now also builds A9Snap_<version>_x64.msix , the same program in an MSIX package that Microsoft signs after it passes certification, so a Store install has no unknown-publisher warning and Windows does the updating. The installer from a9snap.com and its updater are unchanged. The Store version behaves like a Store app. It makes no update check and shows no update controls ( Updates and about says "Updates come from the Microsoft Store."); Start at login uses Windows' startup task, off until you switch it on, and the restart recovery from 0.3.2 works the same way; settings and the log live in the app's own folder (the manual says where), your screenshots stay in your screenshots folder. If the installer copy is installed too, the Store version tells you once that the two don't share settings.

0.3.5 · October 27, 2026 OCR capture copies text, not a picture. Press Alt+X , drag around text in the same pixel-precise picker, and the recognized words go on the clipboard as plain text. No PNG is saved and the capture numbering does not move. Text copied confirms it; No text found or a recognition problem leaves the clipboard alone. The hotkey is configurable in Shortcuts, with its own conflict warning, and the tray menu has an OCR capture item. Copy text from an existing capture. Right-click a capture in the recent strip and choose Copy text , or use the editor's new Copy text button. The editor recognizes the picture currently on screen, including an unsaved crop or annotation, and stays open; neither path changes the capture or writes another file. Recognition is completely local. A9 Snap uses Windows' built-in OCR and your installed OCR languages. Pictures go to the recognizer in memory only: no upload, no temporary image or text files, and no recognized text in the log.

0.3.4 · October 27, 2026 Delete a screenshot from Home. Point at a capture in Recent captures and a small red trash can appears in its corner (also when it has the keyboard focus; always visible on a touch screen). Click it, or press Delete on a focused capture: it fades out, the grid fills with the next-newest one, and a note at the bottom says "Deleted snag_0042.png · Undo" for 6 seconds. The file and, if you had edited it, its hidden original in .a9snap go to the Recycle Bin, never away for good, and Undo puts both back under the same names. If Windows can't move the file (another app has it open, say) the capture stays and the note says why. The strip has the same. Delete takes the picked captures (or the focused one) to the Recycle Bin with one "Deleted 3 screenshots · Undo" note, a small trash can shows on a card under the pointer, and the right-click menu's Delete takes the whole selection a card belongs to. A capture deleted from A9 Snap keeps its number while the app is running: deleting the newest one no longer hands its number to the next capture, so "Next file" stays where it was. (Files deleted in Explorer still follow the folder, as before.)

0.3.3 · October 27, 2026 The A9 Snap manual is at a9snap.com/docs : how to capture, the recent captures strip, the editor (and what Save, Save as new and Revert do to your files), every setting, Start at login, keyboard shortcuts, privacy, and what to do when something goes wrong. It has a search box, screenshots, and an "On this page" list on each page. A Manual row in the Home window (under the section menu) opens it in your browser, and a ? button at the top right of every section opens the page for that section. F1 with the Home window in front does the same, and the tray menu has a Manual item above Settings.

0.3.2 · October 27, 2026 A9 Snap comes back after Windows closes it. When Windows closes every app for a Restart that never finishes (or is cancelled), no sign-in follows, so the login entry never fires and A9 Snap stayed gone. Now, when Windows ends the session, A9 Snap sets a one-time task in your own Task Scheduler to start it again two minutes later. If the PC really restarts, the login entry starts it and removes the task; every start removes it. A9 Snap never holds up a shutdown, and asks Windows to restart it after a crash. The switch shows what Windows will really do, not just what was saved. If you turned A9 Snap off in Windows' Startup apps, Shortcuts keeps the switch on and says "Windows has turned this off in Startup apps." with a Fix in Windows button that opens that page. A9 Snap never switches Windows' own setting back on for you. The login entry is checked on every launch. It is written with the program's path in quotes (the install folder has a space in it) and, if it is missing, unquoted, points at another copy (a dev build, an old path) or is out of date after an update, A9 Snap puts it right; if you switch Start at login off, it is removed. The log now says how A9 Snap ended: quit from the tray, Windows ending the session (and whether the session is really ending), a crash, or a normal exit. A launch at login goes straight to the tray: no window, no confirmation, the hotkeys ready. New installs have Start at login on; if you had turned it off, it stays off.

0.3.1 · October 24, 2026 A new Home window replaces the single scrolling Settings page. Double-click the tray icon (or pick Settings in the tray menu) and it opens on Home: a side column with Capture , Recent captures , Editor (opens your newest capture) and Folder buttons, each showing your own hotkey, and a menu of sections: Home, Shortcuts, Saving, Strip and editor, Notifications, Updates and about. 0.3.0 · October 23, 2026 The editor: draw on a capture and send it. Open it from the recent captures strip ( E , a double-click, or right-click → Edit), from the Edit button on the "Copied · …" confirmation, or after every capture (Settings, "Open the editor after every capture", off by default). Tools, each with a key: Arrow (A), Box (B), Ellipse (E), Highlight (H), Text (T), Blur (U), Crop (C), and Select (V). Five colours (Nine Red, Volt, Ink, white, blue) and thin, medium or thick. Every shape stays editable until you save: select it, move it, drag its handles, change its colour, delete it. Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) go back through the whole session. Blur pixelates the region for real: the saved file holds flat blocks, not the picture with a layer on top. Text is Geist with a soft dark outline so it reads on any background. Crop: drag a region, Enter applies, undo brings the whole picture back. Ctrl+wheel zooms, Ctrl+0 is 100 %. Ctrl+S or Done saves over the same file, so the numbering never changes, and puts the result on the clipboard as the picture and as the file ("Saved · … · copied"). Ctrl+Shift+S saves as the next numbered file instead. Esc with unsaved changes asks in the window: Save, Discard or Cancel. The untouched original is kept in a hidden .a9snap folder inside your screenshots folder, so Revert can put it back. The numbering ignores that folder. A capture that was edited shows a small Volt dot in the strip. The original still holds whatever a blur hid, so delete the .a9snap folder before you share the whole screenshots folder. The confirmation toast now stays 3.5 seconds when it has an Edit button, and is a little wider.

0.1.1 · October 23, 2026 Numbering continues an existing folder: the scan ignores case and treats - , _ , a space or nothing as the same separator, and the next file copies the style of the highest-numbered one ( SNAG-7094.png is followed by SNAG-7095.png , whatever prefix Settings says). 0.1.0 · October 23, 2026 First release: press Alt+Z, drag a region (crosshair, bullseye and an 8x loupe help you land on a single pixel), and the picture is on your clipboard and saved as the next numbered PNG in your screenshots folder.

Press Alt+Z, then click a window, press F for the whole screen, or drag a box. The picture is on your clipboard and saved as a numbered file. Use this whenever you want a picture of part of your screen. It works from any app, and it works on every monitor you have.

h: Capture a window, a screen or a region
t: Capture a window, a screen or a region Press Alt + Z and the screen freezes. What you do next decides what you get: Click a window. As you move the pointer, the window under it gets a Volt outline, with its title and its size. Click, and the picture is that window, the way you see it on the frozen screen, without the invisible border Windows puts around it. The picture is cut from the frozen screen, so it shows what you see: if another window overlaps it, the overlap is in the picture too. Click the bare desktop, or press F . You get the whole monitor the pointer is on. Over the desktop the whole monitor is outlined and labelled Screen , so you can see what a click will take. Drag a box. You get exactly the region you drag. The window outline goes away as soon as you start to drag. A hint at the bottom of the monitor you are on lists these keys: Click a window · Drag a region · F full screen · Esc cancel . It stays for the first few seconds of every capture, and on screen the whole time for your first five captures. A window that stretches over two monitors is cut to the monitor you click on. A maximized window is captured without the taskbar. Pressing Alt + X uses the same picker, so you can click a window to copy its text.

Capture a region Press Alt + Z . Every monitor freezes and dims. A crosshair, a small bullseye and a magnifier follow your pointer. Move to one corner of what you want. Press the mouse button and drag to the opposite corner. The box stays bright. Four Volt corner marks frame it, and a readout shows its size, such as 640 × 220. A tiny drag, under 4 pixels, is a click, and takes the window or screen instead. Let go. The picture is on your clipboard and saved as the next numbered file in your screenshots folder. Dragging a region. The pointer is at the bottom right corner, and the magnifier shows the pixels under it. A note appears at the bottom right of the monitor you captured, for example Copied · snag_0042.png . It goes away by itself after a moment. If you turn the confirmation off in Notifications , problems still show.

Copy text instead with OCR Press Alt + X . The same picker opens. Drag around the text you want and let go. The recognized words go on your clipboard as plain text. Paste them with Ctrl + V . A9 Snap says Text copied , or No text found when it could not read anything. OCR capture saves no picture and no numbered file, and it does not change your next file name. A problem or no text leaves your previous clipboard contents alone. Recognition uses Windows' built-in OCR and the OCR languages installed on your PC. Nothing is uploaded. To copy text from a picture you already took, right-click it in the strip and choose Copy text , or use Copy text in the editor .

Land on the exact pixel The magnifier is a circle that shows the pixels under your pointer at 8 times their size, with a thin grid. The crosshair sits on the edge between pixels, so the sides of your box fall on pixel edges. The magnifier also shows the pointer's position in pixels. It moves to the other side of the pointer when you get near an edge of the screen. Tip: press and hold at the first corner, look at the magnifier, and nudge the pointer until the corner is exactly where you want it. Then drag.

Cancel You can cancel any of these ways. Nothing is copied or saved. Press Esc . Right-click. A click no longer cancels: it takes the window under the pointer, or the screen. If you pressed Alt + Z by accident, press Esc .

Several monitors A9 Snap freezes all your monitors at their real resolution, so a screenshot is sharp even with display scaling at 125% or 150%. The crosshair, bullseye and magnifier are drawn only on the monitor your pointer is on. A capture comes from one monitor: the one where you press the mouse button. If you drag past its edge, the box stops at the edge.

After you let go The clipboard holds the picture. Paste it with Ctrl + V into most apps. If an app wants a file, turn on Also copy as file in Saving . The file is saved as the next number in your screenshots folder. See Where screenshots go . The note is a button. Click Edit on it to draw on the picture. Click the note itself to open the recent captures strip with this capture selected. Hold Shift and click it to show the file in its folder. To open the editor after every capture without clicking, turn on Open the editor after every capture in Strip and editor .

If the hotkey does nothing Another app may own Alt + Z or Alt + X . A9 Snap tells you instead of failing quietly: a warning badge appears on the tray icon and Settings says the key is taken by another app. Pick another. Choose a different key in Shortcuts .

Pictures are saved as numbered PNG files in one folder, and the numbering picks up where the folder left off. Every capture is saved to your screenshots folder as a PNG, as well as going to the clipboard. This page covers the folder, the file names and the clipboard option. All of it lives in Saving on the Home window. The Saving section, showing the folder, the next file name and the clipboard option.

Choose the folder By default A9 Snap saves to Screenshots on your Desktop ( %USERPROFILE%\Desktop\Screenshots ). The folder is made when the first picture is saved. Open the Home window and choose Saving . Next to Screenshots folder , click Browse… and pick a folder. Click Open any time to see the folder in Explorer. To go back, click Use the default folder . The same Folder button is on the Home window's left side, and Open screenshots folder is in the tray menu.

File names and numbering New files are named snag_0042.png : a prefix, a number and .png . The first picture in an empty folder is snag_0001.png . A9 Snap reads the folder on every capture. The new number is the highest one it finds, plus one. It never fills gaps and never overwrites a file. If you delete snag_0007.png , the next capture is still the highest number plus one. When you delete the newest capture from A9 Snap (the trash can or Delete ), its number also stays taken until A9 Snap restarts, so the next capture doesn't reuse it. It counts only files named like your prefix, with the number after it and .png at the end. It ignores letter case, and treats - , _ , a space or nothing between the prefix and the number as the same. With the prefix snag_ , it counts snag_0042.png , SNAG-7094.png and Snag 12.png . It does not count IMG_0042.png or notes.png . If the folder already has such a sequence, the next file copies the style of the highest-numbered one: the same letter case, the same separator and the same number of digits. A folder whose newest file is SNAG-7094.png gets SNAG-7095.png next, whatever the prefix in Settings says. The File name row has two boxes. Prefix is the text before the number (the default is snag_ ). Digits is how many digits the number is padded to with zeros, from 0 to 6, and 0 means no padding. They are used while the folder has no numbered files yet; after that the folder's own style wins. A line under File name shows Next file with the real name, read from your folder as you change things. A prefix can't be empty and can't contain \ / : * ? " < > | .

Also copy as file Most apps paste a picture straight from the clipboard. A few want an attachment instead, such as some chat and email apps. Turn on Also copy as file and the saved file goes on the clipboard too, next to the picture. Apps take whichever they understand. It is off by default.

When something can't be saved If the folder is not writable or the disk is full, you still get the picture on your clipboard. The note says Copied · not saved and gives the reason, and it stays for five seconds even if you turned confirmations off. Pick a different folder in Saving .

One key shows your newest captures as thumbnails. Pick some and copy them, drag them into a chat, or open one to draw on it. The strip is for the moment after you have taken a few screenshots and want to send some of them. It shows your newest captures, newest first, taken from the screenshots folder. The strip with three captures picked. The Copy button says what one click will copy.

Open the strip Do any one of these: Press Alt + Shift + Z . Choose Recent captures from the tray menu. Click Recent captures or Open the strip on the Home window. Click the note that appears after a capture. The strip opens with that capture already selected. The strip appears near the bottom of the monitor your pointer is on. It opens at once with placeholders, and the thumbnails fill in a moment later. Thumbnails are kept in memory only and never written to disk. To change the hotkey, see Shortcuts .

Pick captures and copy them Select a capture. Click it, or press its number, 1 to 9. Click again to unselect. You can pick as many as you like. Press Enter or Ctrl + C , or click the Volt Copy to clipboard button at the top. The button says what a click will copy, such as Copy 3 to clipboard , and reads Select captures to copy until you pick something. Paste with Ctrl + V where you want them. What lands on the clipboard depends on how many you picked: One capture goes as the picture plus its file, so it pastes into an image box or an attachment box. Several captures go as files, oldest first, so they paste in the order you took them. Nothing selected: Enter copies the capture that has the focus ring. A note says Copied 4 captures and the strip closes. To move around with the keyboard, use the arrow keys, Home and End . Space picks or unpicks the focused capture, and Ctrl + A picks all of them.

Search your captures The strip shows your 12 newest, but the search looks through every capture in the folder. Click the Search captures box at the top, or press Ctrl + F or / . The box does not take the keyboard when the strip opens, so E , Enter , Delete and the arrow keys keep working on the cards until you ask for it. Type part of a file name, such as 07 or snag_01 , or the app or the window title the picture came from , such as chrome or quarterly budget . It ignores capital letters. The strip lists every capture that matches, newest first, and says how many ( 48 captures ). See Search by app and window title . The chips under the box narrow the list further: Today , This week (today and the six days before, by the time each file was last saved), Edited (captures you marked up in the editor, the ones with the Volt dot) and up to four app chips . Click a chip to turn it on, and again to turn it off. A chip that is on is Volt. Chips and text work together: both must match. Down , Tab or Enter in the box moves to the first result. Esc in the box clears the text first; press Esc again to close the strip. When nothing matches, the strip says No captures match with a Clear link that turns the search off. Picking, copying, dragging, editing and deleting work the same on the results. The search starts empty each time you open the strip.

h: Search by app and window title
t: Search by app and window title Every file is named snag_0042.png , so A9 Snap also notes which app and window each new capture came from and lets you search by that. A click on a window notes that window. A dragged region notes the topmost window under the middle of the region. The whole screen ( F , or a click on the desktop) notes the window you were working in. The app is its friendly name, such as Google Chrome or Outlook ; the title is the window's title. After Today , This week and Edited , up to four app chips show the apps you capture most. They say Chrome and Outlook , not Google Chrome and Microsoft Outlook . They work like the other chips and are hidden until at least one capture has an app. Point at a capture to see App · title in its tooltip. Captures from before 0.5.2 have no app. They are still found by file name, date and Edited . The notes are kept in .a9snap\captures.json , the hidden folder inside your screenshots folder, next to the originals of edited captures. Window titles can contain an email subject or a document's name. They stay on this PC, are never sent anywhere and never go into the log. To stop noting them, turn off Remember which app each capture came from in Saving ; the Clear button beside it deletes what is already noted. See Privacy .

Scroll to the rest The strip keeps its rows the same height and scrolls . With a search or a chip on, every match is reachable: use the mouse wheel, the arrow keys past the last row, or PageUp and PageDown . The line under the chips says 48 captures when you can scroll to all of them, and Showing 12 of 48 when the strip is only showing your newest. Thumbnails load as the captures scroll into view.

Edit a capture Press E to open the picked capture in the editor . If you picked none or several, E opens the one with the focus ring. Double-clicking a capture does the same. A small Volt dot next to a name means the capture has been edited and its original is kept.

The right-click menu Right-click a capture for: Edit opens it in the editor. Copy text recognizes the text in the picture with Windows' built-in OCR and puts it on the clipboard as plain text. It changes no file. A9 Snap says Text copied , or No text found if there was nothing to read. Open opens the file in your default picture app. Show in folder opens Explorer with the file selected. Copy path puts the file's full path on the clipboard. Delete moves the file to the Recycle Bin. If the capture is part of a larger selection, the whole selection goes.

Delete a screenshot Three ways, all the same: Point at a capture and click the small red trash can that appears in its top-right corner. Pick one or more captures and press Delete . With nothing picked, Delete removes the capture with the focus ring. Choose Delete in the right-click menu. The captures go to the Recycle Bin, not away for good, and so does the hidden original the editor kept for an edited one. The strip stays open and fills the space with the next capture. A note says Deleted snag_0042.png , or Deleted 3 screenshots , with an Undo button for 6 seconds. Undo puts the files back under the same names, exactly as they were. After that you can still restore them from the Recycle Bin. A deleted capture keeps its number while A9 Snap is running, so the next capture is never given the number of the one you just threw away. If Windows can't move a file, because another app has it open, the capture stays and the note says why.

Drag captures out Drag one capture, or the whole selection, out of the strip. They go as files, so you can drop them into Explorer, a browser chat box, Teams or Outlook. If the capture you drag is part of a larger selection, the whole selection goes.
Close the strip Press Esc (twice if the search box has text in it), click anywhere outside it, or press the hotkey again. Closing never touches your clipboard.

h: How many captures it shows, and how many to a row
t: How many captures it shows, and how many to a row The strip shows 12 captures by default, and the search reaches the rest. Captures in the strip in Strip and editor can be 6, 9, 12, 18 or 24, and Per row can be 4, 6, 8 or 12. The default is 12 captures, 6 to a row: two rows of six. The strip is centred on the monitor your pointer is on and never wider than its work area: if a row doesn't fit, it holds fewer, and if the rows don't fit the height, you scroll. The strip lists only files named like your prefix, such as snag_0042.png . See Where screenshots go .
Where to go next Mark up a screenshot Keyboard shortcuts Settings sections

Open a capture in the editor and add an arrow, a box, some text, a highlight, a blur or a crop, then send it. The editor is deliberately small. It has seven tools and nothing more, so marking up a screenshot takes a few seconds. Everything you draw stays editable until you save. The editor on a mock capture: a box, an arrow and a text label, with the toolbar above.

h: Open a capture in the editor
t: Open a capture in the editor Pick whichever is closest: In the strip , select a capture and press E , double-click it, or right-click it and choose Edit . Click Edit on the note that appears after a capture. On the Home window, click one of the six captures, or click Editor to open the newest capture. Turn on Open the editor after every capture in Strip and editor to open it automatically.

Draw something Choose a tool from the toolbar, or press its key. Drag on the picture. A line under the picture tells you what the tool does. Pick a colour and a width in the toolbar. They apply to what you draw next. Keep going, then press Ctrl + S or click Done to save. See Saving, Save as new and Revert . The colours are Nine Red, Volt, Ink, White and Blue. The widths are Thin, Medium and Thick. The highlighter starts out Volt.

The tools Tool Key What it does Select V Click a shape to select it, drag to move it, drag its handles to resize it. Change its colour or width, or press Delete to remove it. Arrow A Drag from the tail to where the head should be. The head is where you let go. Box B Drag out a rectangle outline. Ellipse E Drag out an oval outline. Highlight H Drag over what matters. It paints a translucent band, Volt by default. Text T Click, type, then press Enter to finish. Shift + Enter starts a new line. Esc cancels. The width sets the text size. Blur U Drag over what to hide. It turns the area into flat blocks. Crop C Drag the region to keep, adjust it with the handles, then press Enter . Esc cancels. To fix a text, double-click it. Text uses Geist with a soft dark outline, so it reads on any background.

Blur Blur pixelates for real. The saved file holds flat blocks where the area was, not the picture with a layer on top, so nobody can lift the blur off later. Before you save, undo still brings the pixels back. After you save, see the note on originals .
Crop Drag a region, then press Enter to apply it. The footer shows the new size and the original size. Undo brings the whole picture back until you save.

Copy text Click Copy text in the top bar to recognize the picture currently on screen with Windows' built-in OCR and put the words on the clipboard as plain text. This includes an unsaved crop or annotation, so what you see is what gets recognized. The editor stays open, your document keeps its unsaved state, and no file is written. A9 Snap says Text copied , or No text found when there was nothing to read.

Undo, redo and zoom Ctrl + Z undoes. Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z redoes. They go back through the whole session, not just the last shape. Ctrl +scroll zooms around the pointer. Ctrl + 0 shows the picture at 100%. The zoom button in the top bar switches between fit and 100%. Scroll to move around a zoomed picture. You can also hold Space and drag, or drag with the middle button.
Where to go next Saving, Save as new and Revert The recent captures strip Keyboard shortcuts

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
h: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Save over the capture, save as a new numbered file, or go back to the original. Here is exactly what each one does to your files. When you finish drawing, you have two ways to save and one way back. This page explains each, and what happens to the untouched original.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Save over the capture Press Ctrl + S or click Done . A9 Snap keeps the untouched original first, if it has not already (see Where originals are kept ). It writes your edit over the same file, under the same name. The numbering never changes. It puts the result on the clipboard, as the picture and as the file, just like a capture. A note says Saved · snag_0042.png · copied , and the editor closes. If you did not change anything, Done just closes the editor and writes nothing.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Save as new Press Ctrl + Shift + S or click Save as new . The edit is saved as the next numbered file, the highest number plus one, in the folder's own style. The original capture is left exactly as it was. The result goes on the clipboard and the note says Saved as · snag_0043.png · copied . Use this when you want to keep both the plain screenshot and the marked-up one.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Close without saving Press Esc . If you have changes that are not saved, the editor asks inside its own window: Save your changes? with three buttons. The question the editor asks when you close with unsaved changes. Save saves over the capture, like Done . Enter chooses it. Discard closes and keeps the file as it was. Cancel goes back to editing. Esc chooses it. Esc works from the inside out: it first leaves a text you are typing, then a drag, then a crop waiting for Enter , and only then asks about closing.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Revert Revert puts the original picture back. It shows in the top bar only when the capture has an original to go back to, which means you have saved an edit over it at least once. Open the edited capture in the editor . Click Revert . Read Go back to the original? It says the file is replaced by the picture as it was captured and that your edits to it are lost. Click Revert to confirm, or Cancel . A note says Reverted · snag_0042.png . The original is removed from its hidden folder once it is back, so a second Revert has nothing to go back to until you save another edit.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Where originals are kept The first time you save an edit over a capture, A9 Snap copies the untouched picture into a hidden folder named .a9snap inside your screenshots folder. The copy is named like snag_0042.orig.png . A second edit keeps the first original, never an earlier edit. The numbering ignores that folder, so editing changes no number. The strip and the Home window show an edited capture with a small Volt dot. Deleting a capture with the trash can or Delete sends its hidden original to the Recycle Bin with it, and Undo brings both back. Deleting the file in Explorer leaves the original behind. Save as new creates a file with no original of its own, because the plain capture is still there.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
h: Blur is permanent in the saved file
t: Blur is permanent in the saved file A blur turns the area into flat blocks in the file you save. The pixels it hid are gone from that file. But the original, which is the picture before any edit, still holds them, and it stays in .a9snap until you Revert or delete it. Before you share a whole screenshots folder, delete the .a9snap folder inside it. Sharing a single file is safe, because the original is not inside that file.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Where to go next Mark up a screenshot The recent captures strip Privacy

The one window A9 Snap has: your actions on the left, your newest captures in the middle, and every setting a click away. Open the Home window by double-clicking the tray icon, or by choosing Settings in the tray menu. It always opens on Home, however you left it. Closing the window does not quit A9 Snap: it keeps waiting in the tray. The Home window on mock captures.

The left side Capture starts a screenshot, just like the hotkey. Your capture hotkey shows on the button. Recent captures opens the strip . Its hotkey shows on the button. Editor opens your newest capture in the editor . It is dimmed until you have a capture. Folder opens your screenshots folder in Explorer. The menu of sections has Home, Shortcuts, Saving, Strip and editor, Notifications and Updates and about. Click one, or use the up and down arrow keys. See Settings sections . Manual opens this manual in your browser. It sits under the menu of sections. When an update is waiting, a card appears with Update now . It restarts A9 Snap and takes a few seconds. At the bottom is the version and channel, for example v0.3.3 · Dev , with Up to date beside it when that is so.

The middle Ready when you are reminds you of the hotkey and shows Running in the tray . Recent captures shows your six newest captures as thumbnails, with the file name, how long ago you took each, and a Volt dot on edited ones. Click one to open it in the editor. Open the strip shows more. With no captures yet it says where to start. Saving to shows your screenshots folder and Next file , the name the next capture will get. After a capture says what happens when you let go: Copied as an image , Copied as image and file , and Opens in the editor if you turned that on.

Delete a screenshot Point at a capture in Recent captures and a small red trash can appears in the top-right corner of its picture. It also shows when the capture has the keyboard focus. Click it, or press Delete with the capture focused, and: The capture fades out and the grid fills in with the next-newest one. A note at the bottom of the window says Deleted snag_0042.png with an Undo button, for 6 seconds. The file goes to the Recycle Bin, not away for good, and so does the hidden original the editor kept if you had edited it. Undo puts both back under the same names, exactly as they were, and the capture returns to the grid. Clicking the trash can never opens the editor. Next file doesn't change: a deleted capture keeps its number while A9 Snap is running, so the next capture is never given the number of the one you just threw away. If Windows can't move the file, for example because another app has it open, the capture stays and the note says why. The strip works the same way.

The ? buttons and F1 Every section, including Home, has a ? button at the top right. It opens the manual page for that section. Start at login has a small ? of its own. With the Home window in front, press F1 for the page that matches the section on screen. The tray menu's Manual item opens the front page.
The size of the window It opens at 1000 × 680 and can be made as small as 860 × 600. At the smallest size the right-hand side scrolls.
Where to go next Settings sections Start at login Take a screenshot

Every setting, section by section, in the order the Home window lists them, with what each one does and its default. Every setting is in the Home window's menu of sections. Each section has a ? button at the top right that opens its manual page. A change is saved the moment you make it, and A9 Snap checks it. If a value is not allowed, a line under the setting says why and the setting goes back to what it was. For the window itself, see The Home window .

Shortcuts The Shortcuts section. Capture hotkey starts a screenshot. Default Alt + Z . OCR capture hotkey copies recognized text from a region without saving a picture. Default Alt + X . Recent captures hotkey opens the strip . Default Alt + Shift + Z . Start at login starts A9 Snap in the tray when you sign in to Windows. On by default for a new install. See Start at login . To change a hotkey: Click the box. It says Press the keys… Press the combination you want, for example Ctrl + Alt + P . If the key is allowed and free, it is saved. Press Esc to leave the box without changing it. A hotkey needs Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win with a key. Function keys and PrintScreen may stand alone. The three hotkeys must all be different. A9 Snap never takes Ctrl + Alt + S , Win + Shift + S or Ctrl + C , V , X and Z . They belong to Windows and to every app's editing keys. If another app already owns a key, the box is marked and a line says Alt+Z is taken by another app. Pick another. The tray icon also shows a warning badge until you fix it.

Saving The Saving section. Screenshots folder is where pictures are saved. Default Desktop\Screenshots . Browse… picks another, Open shows it, Use the default folder goes back. File name has Prefix (default snag_ ) and Digits (default 4, from 0 to 6). A line shows Next file . Remember which app each capture came from notes the app and window title of each new capture so the strip can search by them. On by default. Window titles can contain an email subject or a document's name; they stay in the hidden .a9snap folder in your screenshots folder and never leave this PC. Turning it off stops new notes and keeps the old ones; Clear next to it deletes them. See Privacy . Also copy as file puts the saved file on the clipboard next to the picture. Off by default. Where screenshots go explains the numbering in full.

Strip and editor The Strip and editor section. Captures in the strip is how many of the newest captures the strip shows: 6, 9, 12, 18 or 24. Default 12. A search finds all of them, however many. Per row is how many of them sit in one row: 4, 6, 8 or 12. Default 6, so 12 captures make two rows of six. A narrow screen gets fewer to a row, and a short one scrolls. Open the editor after every capture opens the editor on each capture as you take it. Off by default. When it is off, press E in the strip or click Edit on the note.

Notifications The Notifications section. Show a confirmation shows a small note at the bottom right after each capture, such as Copied · snag_0042.png . On by default. The note stays about a second and a half, or three and a half seconds when it has an Edit button. Problems always show, and stay for five seconds, whatever this setting says.

Updates and about The Updates and about section. Version shows the number you have, your channel and when the last check got an answer. Check for updates looks now. When an update is ready the button becomes Update now . Update channel is Dev or Stable . See Updates and channels . What's new shows the newest change in a sentence. Release notes opens this version's notes on GitHub. All versions are in What's new . In the Microsoft Store version there is no Check for updates button and no Update channel : the row says Updates come from the Microsoft Store. At the bottom, a line reminds you that nothing leaves your PC except the update check. See Privacy .
Where to go next Start at login Keyboard shortcuts If something goes wrong

A9 Snap can start by itself when you sign in to Windows, so your hotkey is always ready. Here is how it behaves, and what to do when Windows says no. Start at login is on for a new install, in the downloaded version and the Microsoft Store version alike. A9 Snap starts straight into the tray: no window opens and nothing asks you anything. If you had turned it off before, it stays off.

The Microsoft Store version The Microsoft Store version starts at login through Windows' own startup task instead of a startup entry, because a Store app's startup entry would never reach Windows. It is on for a new install, the same as the downloaded version, but the Store doesn't launch the app for you: open A9 Snap once after installing , and that first launch switches the startup task on. Settings › Apps › Startup in Windows then shows A9 Snap with its switch on. The Start at login switch turns the task on and off. If you turn it off in Windows, A9 Snap says so and Fix in Windows opens that page, exactly as below; if an administrator's policy turned it off, the same line shows, and A9 Snap never tries to override either. A login start is quiet, as with the downloaded version: no window, only the tray icon. The restart recovery described at the bottom of this page works the same way in the Store version: the one-time task starts A9 Snap through its app execution alias ( a9snap.exe in your WindowsApps folder), because Task Scheduler can't start a Store app by the path of its program file.

Turn it on or off Open the Home window and choose Shortcuts . Use the Start at login switch. Turning it on adds a startup entry for your Windows user, with the program's path in quotes (the install folder has a space in it). Turning it off removes the entry.

What the switch shows The switch shows what Windows will really do, not only what you saved. Windows has its own list in Settings › Apps › Startup , and it can turn A9 Snap off there. If Windows turned it off, the switch stays on and a line under it says Windows has turned this off in Startup apps. Click Fix in Windows . It opens that Windows page. Turn A9 Snap on there. A9 Snap never switches Windows' own setting back on for you. If A9 Snap could not add its startup entry, the line says A9 Snap couldn't add itself to Windows startup. What you see when Windows has turned A9 Snap off in Startup apps.

It checks itself A9 Snap checks its startup entry every time it starts. If the entry is missing, has no quotes, points at another copy (an old path or a development build) or is out of date after an update, A9 Snap puts it right. If you switch the setting off, the entry is removed.

h: After Windows closes your apps for an update
t: After Windows closes your apps for an update Sometimes Windows closes every app so it can restart for an update, and then the restart never finishes, or you cancel it. Nothing signs you in again, so the startup entry never fires and A9 Snap would stay closed. To cover that, when Windows ends your session and Start at login is on, A9 Snap sets a one-time task in your own Task Scheduler named A9 Snap relaunch after Windows closed it . It starts A9 Snap again two minutes later and ends after an hour. If the PC really restarts, the startup entry starts A9 Snap and removes the task. Every start of A9 Snap removes the task. A9 Snap never holds up a shutdown or a restart, and it asks Windows to start it again after a crash. With Start at login off, no task is made.

Checking what happened The log file records how each run ended: quit from the tray, Windows ending the session (and whether the session is really ending), a crash, or a normal exit. A login start is recorded as started at login .
Where to go next Settings sections If something goes wrong

Every key A9 Snap uses, what each does, its default, and where you can change it. A9 Snap has two kinds of keys. Global hotkeys work from any app, even when no A9 Snap window is open. You can change these. Window keys work only while the strip or the editor is in front. These are fixed. Keys are written like Alt + Z , which means hold Alt and press Z .

Global hotkeys Change all three in Shortcuts . Key Default What it does Capture hotkey Alt + Z Freezes the screen. Click a window, press F for the whole screen, or drag a region. OCR capture hotkey Alt + X Copies recognized text from a region, without saving a picture. Recent captures hotkey Alt + Shift + Z Opens the strip . Press it again to close the strip.

h: While you pick (after Alt + Z or Alt + X )
t: While you pick (after Alt + Z or Alt + X ) Key What it does Click Takes the window under the pointer (it is outlined). Over the bare desktop, takes the whole monitor. F Takes the whole monitor the pointer is on. Drag Takes the region you drag. Esc Cancels. Nothing is copied or saved. Right-click Cancels.

In the recent captures strip See The recent captures strip . Key What it does 1 to 9 Picks or unpicks that capture. Arrow keys, Home , End Move the focus ring. Space Picks or unpicks the focused capture. Ctrl + A Picks all of them. Enter or Ctrl + C Copies the picked captures, or the focused one if none are picked. E Opens the picked capture, or the focused one, in the editor. Delete Moves the picked captures, or the focused one, to the Recycle Bin. The note has an Undo button. Ctrl + F or / Searches : puts the keyboard in the search box. Esc Closes the strip. In the search box it clears the text first. Down , Tab or Enter in the search box Moves on to the first result.

In the editor See Mark up a screenshot and Saving, Save as new and Revert . Key What it does V Select tool. A Arrow. B Box. E Ellipse. H Highlight. T Text. U Blur. C Crop. Ctrl + Z Undo. Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z Redo. Delete or Backspace Removes the selected shape. Enter Finishes a text or applies a crop. Shift + Enter New line in a text. Ctrl + S Saves over the capture, copies it and closes. Same as Done . Ctrl + Shift + S Saves as the next numbered file. Same as Save as new . Ctrl + 0 Shows the picture at 100%. Ctrl +scroll Zooms around the pointer. Space +drag Moves around a zoomed picture. Esc Leaves a text, a drag or a crop first. With unsaved changes it then asks Save your changes? Otherwise it closes.

In the Home window Key What it does ↑ and ↓ Move through the menu of sections, once a section in the menu has the focus. Delete On a capture in Recent captures: moves it to the Recycle Bin. The note at the bottom has an Undo button. F1 Opens the manual page for the section on screen, in your browser.

Keys A9 Snap never takes A hotkey needs a modifier ( Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win ), except function keys and PrintScreen . A9 Snap refuses these, because they belong to Windows or to every app's editing keys: Win + Shift + S , Windows' own screen snipping. Ctrl + Alt + S . Ctrl + C , Ctrl + V , Ctrl + X and Ctrl + Z . The three global hotkeys must all be different keys.
Where to go next Settings sections If something goes wrong

Fixes for the problems people hit most: a hotkey that does nothing, a picture that won't paste, a missing tray icon, and an update that fails. Find your problem below. If none of it helps, the log file says what A9 Snap did.

h: A hotkey is taken by another app
t: A hotkey is taken by another app What you see: pressing Alt + Z does nothing, the tray icon wears a warning badge, and Settings says Alt+Z is taken by another app. Pick another. Another program already owns that key, and Windows lets only one program have it. Open the Home window and choose Shortcuts . Click the box that is marked, then press a different combination, such as Ctrl + Alt + P . The same goes for OCR capture hotkey and Recent captures hotkey . If you would rather keep the key, close or reconfigure the other app first, then restart A9 Snap.

h: Nothing is on the clipboard, or it won't paste
t: Nothing is on the clipboard, or it won't paste Read the note. Copied · snag_0042.png means the picture is on the clipboard. Saved snag_0042.png · not copied gives the reason it was not. These notes show for five seconds, even with confirmations off. Try another app. Paste into Paint or a document. If it works there, the first app wants a file instead of a picture: turn on Also copy as file in Saving . Check a clipboard tool. A clipboard manager or a remote desktop session can hold the clipboard for a moment. Try again. Use the strip. Press Alt + Shift + Z , pick the capture and press Enter to copy it again as a picture plus its file.

h: OCR finds no text or cannot start
t: OCR finds no text or cannot start No text found means Windows could not read words in the selected picture. Try a tighter region around clear, upright text, or a larger region with less background. Your previous clipboard contents are unchanged. If the note says Windows OCR is unavailable for your profile's languages, install an OCR-capable language in Windows Settings under Time & language → Language & region , then try again. OCR is local. A9 Snap does not send the picture to an online service, so this does not require an account or an API key.

The picture wasn't saved The note says Copied · not saved with a reason, for example that the folder can't be written to or the disk is full. The picture is still on your clipboard, so paste it now. Then pick a folder you can write to in Saving .

The next number is wrong The number is the highest file in the folder plus one, counting only files named like your prefix. If you moved or deleted files, it follows the folder. See File names and numbering .

h: A9 Snap did not start after a restart
t: A9 Snap did not start after a restart Open the Home window (from the Start menu, if the tray icon is missing) and choose Shortcuts . Check that Start at login is on. If a line says Windows has turned this off in Startup apps. , click Fix in Windows and turn A9 Snap on there. If Windows closed your apps for an update and the restart never finished, A9 Snap starts again by itself two minutes later. See Start at login .

h: I can't find the tray icon
t: I can't find the tray icon Click the ^ arrow by the clock to show hidden icons. You can drag the Bullseye out onto the taskbar to keep it visible. If it isn't there, start A9 Snap from the Start menu.

h: Windows says it protected your PC
t: Windows says it protected your PC This happens with the installer from a9snap.com, not with the Microsoft Store version. The steps are in Getting started , under If your work PC blocks the Microsoft Store .

An update failed The Home window's version line says Check failed , and the line under Version in Updates and about says why. Couldn't reach the update server. means your network, a firewall or a proxy blocked the check. The update didn't pass its signature check, so it was not installed. means the download was damaged or changed on the way, and A9 Snap refused it. Open Updates and about and click Check for updates again. A9 Snap checks on launch and every few hours, so a short outage fixes itself. Make sure your network or firewall allows raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com . See Privacy . If it still fails, download the installer again from a9snap.com and run it. It updates your copy and keeps your settings.

Where the log file is A9 Snap writes a log to a9snap.log in this folder: %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9snap\logs Press Win + R , paste that folder path and press Enter to open it. The log records starts and exits, hotkey conflicts, update checks, sizes, timings and the reasons for errors. It never contains the content of your screenshots. Your settings are in settings.json in the folder above it. If you installed A9 Snap from the Microsoft Store, Windows keeps those files inside the app's own folder instead. Press Win + R , type %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages and press Enter , open the folder that starts with Atlas9LLC.A9Snap_ , then LocalCache\Roaming\ai.atlas9.a9snap\logs . Your screenshots are not there: they stay in your screenshots folder, whichever way you installed A9 Snap.
Where to go next Keyboard shortcuts Start at login Privacy
Nothing leaves your PC except the update check. No account, no telemetry, no uploads. A9 Snap is built to stay on your computer. This page lists everything it stores and everything it sends.

What leaves your PC Only the update check, and the Microsoft Store version of A9 Snap does not even make that: the Store updates it. See The update check . A9 Snap has no account, no sign-in, no analytics and no crash reporting. It never uploads a screenshot anywhere.

The update check On launch and every few hours, A9 Snap asks one public file whether a newer version exists. The file is channels/dev.json or channels/stable.json , depending on your channel , at raw.githubusercontent.com in the A9 Snap releases repository on GitHub. If there is a newer version, A9 Snap downloads the installer from that same repository's releases and checks its signature before it will install anything. Those requests carry the normal information any web request does, such as your IP address. They carry no screenshot, no file name and no setting.

h: What is stored on your PC
t: What is stored on your PC Screenshots go to the clipboard and to your screenshots folder, and nowhere else. Thumbnails for the strip and the Home window are made in memory and never written to disk. OCR uses Windows' built-in recognizer on your PC. The picture goes to it in memory only, and the recognized text goes only to the clipboard when you ask for it. An OCR capture saves no PNG. There are no temporary image or text files and no recognized text in the log. Originals of edited captures are kept in a hidden .a9snap folder inside your screenshots folder. After a blur, the saved file has the pixels destroyed but the original still holds them. See Blur is permanent in the saved file . Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. Which app each capture came from is noted in .a9snap\captures.json , in the same hidden folder next to the originals. For each new capture it holds the file name, size and time, the app's name (such as Google Chrome) and the window's title, so the strip can search by them. Window titles can contain an email subject or a document's name. The notes stay in your screenshots folder, never leave this PC and never go into the log. Turn them off with Remember which app each capture came from in Saving , and press Clear there to delete what is already noted. Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. Secure capture, when it arrives, will never note them. Settings are in settings.json in %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9snap . The log is in the logs folder beside it. It records sizes, timings and status codes, never the content of a screenshot, a file or recognized text. Start at login adds one startup entry for your Windows user, and a one-time Task Scheduler task when Windows ends your session. See Start at login .

This website The manual loads its own fonts and scripts from a9snap.com. It has no analytics and no cookies. The home page loads its fonts from Google Fonts and reads the newest version number from the same GitHub file that the app uses.
Where to go next Updates and channels Saving, Save as new and Revert

How A9 Snap finds and installs new versions, and what the Dev and Stable channels mean. A9 Snap updates itself, but never without you. It checks, downloads in the background, and then waits for you to restart.

The Microsoft Store version If you installed A9 Snap from the Microsoft Store, Windows updates it and A9 Snap does not check for updates itself. There is no Check for updates button, no Update now card, no channel and no update item in the tray menu. Updates and about says Updates come from the Microsoft Store. , and the version line shows your version with Microsoft Store , for example v0.3.6 · Microsoft Store . To look now, open the Microsoft Store, then Library and Get updates . Everything below is about the version you install from a9snap.com.

How an update works A9 Snap checks on launch and every few hours. You can check now with Check for updates in Updates and about , or in the tray menu. If a newer version exists, it downloads it and checks its signature. The Home window shows a card: Downloading 0.3.3… , then Version 0.3.3 is ready . The tray menu says Restart to update to 0.3.3 . Click Update now on the card, or choose the tray item. A9 Snap restarts. It takes a few seconds, and your settings and screenshots are untouched. If you ignore the card, nothing happens. The update waits until you are ready. A failed check never throws away an update that is already downloaded.

Dev and Stable The channel decides which versions you are offered. Dev gets every build. It is the default, and it is how new features reach you first. Stable gets only the builds that were promoted after they had time to prove themselves. To switch, open Updates and about and pick the other one in Update channel . The version line at the bottom left of the Home window shows your channel, for example v0.3.3 · Dev . Switching to Stable never installs an older version. It just waits for the next promoted build.
See what changed Release notes in Updates and about opens your version's notes on GitHub. What's new lists every version in this manual.
